newsitem.title: YEMEN: Royal yacht Britannia docks in Aden on last tour.
newsitem.headline: Royal yacht Britannia docks in Aden on last tour.

text.p: The royal yacht Britannia, a symbol of the days when Britain ruled the waves, arrived in the southern Yemeni port of Aden on Friday en route to Hong Kong on its final voyage.
The sleek 6,000-tonne luxurious mini-liner, which costs about $17 million a year to run, is being taken out of service after the current tour, ending 44 years afloat.

Yemeni Trade Minister Abdul-Rahman Mohammad Ali Othman and Britain's ambassador to Yemen attended a ceremony welcoming Britannia. The yacht docked on Thursday at the Red Sea port of Hodeida at the start of a three-day visit to Yemen, its first port of call in the Middle East.
The ship is due to host a symposium entitled "Invest in Yemen", which has been touted by the local press as a "milestone in Yemeni-U.K. business".

The meeting will be attended by representatives of leading British companies including British Petroleum, British Airways, British Aerospace and defence-to- electronics giant General Electric Co Plc, the British Embassy in Sanaa said in a statement.
Britain is Yemen's second-largest trading partner after the United States.
Until 1967 Britain ruled Aden directly and the rest of Yemen indirectly through a protectorate agreement with local sultans.

The Britannia has been to Yemen, an impoverished small oil-producer country with 16 million people, seven times between 1959 and 1993. On its fourth visit in 1986, it helped evacuate hundreds of Britons and other foreign nationals during clashes in former South Yemen.
The Britannia is due to leave Yemen on Sunday and head to the Gulf, where it will make visits to the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Kuwait and Bahrain.
